title: Companies, Business Trusts and Other Bodies (Miscellaneous Amendments) Bill
what_it_is: Companies, Business Trusts and Other Bodies (Miscellaneous Amendments) Bill

sections.label: Permanent virtual and hybrid meetings
sections.summary: Amendments to several Acts permanently give companies, business trusts and variable capital companies the option of fully virtual or hybrid meetings.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: The fourth set of amendments, which applies to several Acts, permanently provides companies, business trusts and variable capital companies with the option to conduct fully virtual or hybrid meetings.

sections.label: Excluded persons in acquisition threshold
sections.summary: Three additional categories of persons are excluded when computing the 90% compulsory acquisition threshold.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: Specifically, three additional categories of persons will be excluded when computing the 90% compulsory acquisition threshold.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: These three categories are: (a) bodies corporate who are controlled by the buyer; (b) persons who are controlled or can be influenced by the buyer to approve of his takeover offer, for example, his close relatives and bodies corporate controlled by such persons; and (c) persons who control the buyer and the bodies corporate controlled by such persons.

sections.label: Disqualification periods for directors
sections.summary: The Bill reduces the disqualification period for first-time disqualified directors to three years and keeps it at five years for repeat directors.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: To better reflect the culpability of a disqualified director, the Bill will reduce the disqualification period for first-time disqualified directors to three years, while keeping that for repeat disqualified directors at five years.

sections.label: Raised maximum penalties
sections.summary: Maximum penalties are raised to $250,000 without intent to defraud, and to $250,000 and three years' imprisonment with intent to defraud.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: The maximum penalty for cases where there is no intent to defraud will be raised to $250,000.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: The maximum penalty for offences where there is intent to defraud will be raised to $250,000 and three years' imprisonment.

sections.label: Virtual meetings from July 2023
sections.summary: Enabling provisions clarify that companies, business trusts and variable capital companies may hold hybrid or fully virtual meetings from 1 July 2023.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: To continue enabling virtual or hybrid meetings, in addition to the physical meetings which they are already able to hold under existing legislation, we will make enabling provisions to clarify that companies, business trusts and variable capital companies may conduct their meetings, including general meetings in a hybrid or fully virtual manner from 1 July 2023.

sections.label: Responsible operation and virtual meetings
sections.summary: This ensures companies operate responsibly and ethically for long-term stakeholder value, and lets companies and other corporate entities hold virtual or hybrid general meetings.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: This ensures that the companies operate in a responsible and ethical manner with a focus on creating long-term value for all stakeholders.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: This Bill will allow companies and other corporate entities to conduct virtual or hybrid general meetings.

sections.label: Court invalidating disrupted meetings
sections.summary: New section 392(2A) lets the Court declare a meeting invalid for technological disruption, malfunction or outage causing substantial injustice that cannot be remedied.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: The new section 392(2A) allows the Court to declare a meeting invalid if there is a technological disruption, malfunction or outage that has or may cause substantial injustice that cannot be remedied.

sections.label: New offences for meeting disruption
sections.summary: The question asks whether the Ministry has considered new offences for individuals who disrupt meetings intending to invalidate the proceedings.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Can the Minister share if the Ministry has considered the need to introduce new offences for individuals who take steps to disrupt meetings with the intention that the meeting proceedings be invalidated?

sections.label: Three meeting scenarios
sections.summary: The amendments provide for meetings to be held at a physical place, as a hybrid meeting, or using virtual technology only.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: The amendments provide for meetings to held in three scenarios: one, at a physical place; two, at a physical place and using virtual meeting concurrently, that is, a hybrid meeting; and three, just using virtual technology only.

sections.label: Virtual AGMs after COVID provisions
sections.summary: The proposed amendments will allow companies to hold AGMs and shareholder meetings virtually even after the COVID-19 provisions are revoked in July.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: The proposed amendments will allow companies to hold their AGMs and shareholder meetings virtually, even after the enabling COVID-19 provisions allowing virtual meetings are revoked in July.

sections.label: Hybrid meetings and jurisdiction question
sections.summary: The speaker favours keeping the hybrid meeting option open but notes the Bill does not address where virtual or hybrid meetings are deemed held jurisdictionally.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: I certainly favour keeping such an option open and I would agree with my resident that allowing hybrid meetings may well boost overall attendance.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: I note that the Bill does not seem to address the issue of where any such virtual or hybrid meetings would be deemed to be held jurisdictionally.

sections.label: Shareholders applying to invalidate meetings
sections.summary: New section 392(2A) under clause 15 lets shareholders apply to the Court to invalidate a company's meeting if technological disruptions cause substantial injustice.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: As I had explained in my speech earlier, the new section 392(2A) under clause 15 of the Bill will allow shareholders to apply to the Court for a company's meeting to be invalidated, if they suffer substantial injustice due to disruptions, malfunctions or outages that are technological in nature.

sections.label: No new offences needed
sections.summary: The passage states there is no need to introduce new offences for such a situation at this juncture.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: At this juncture, there is no need to introduce new offences for such a situation.

sections.label: Companies Act meeting jurisdiction
sections.summary: The Companies Act as it stands does not prescribe jurisdictional requirements for where company meetings are deemed held.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: The Companies Act in general, as it currently stands, does not prescribe jurisdictional requirements for where company meetings are deemed to be held.

sections.label: Virtual board meetings clarified
sections.summary: The amendments clarify that nothing in the Companies Act prevents virtual board meetings and do not change the current position.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: Specifically, the amendments only clarify that nothing in the Companies Act prevents board of directors' meetings from being conducted virtually and do not change the current position in the Companies Act where board of directors' meetings may be conducted virtually.

sections.label: Virtual and hybrid meetings option
sections.summary: The amendments let entities hold virtual or hybrid meetings, subject to regulator rules, and permanently give companies, business trusts and variable capital companies that option.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: These amendments will enable entities to conduct virtual or hybrid meetings should they do so and they should be mindful of the regulations issued by the respective regulators.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: So, for example, SGX has publicly communicated that SGX-listed issuers may conduct physical or hybrid general meetings from 1 July 2023 onwards.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: This provides issuers added flexibility to decide the format of meeting that suits their shareholders needs and facilitates shareholder engagement.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: These proposed amendments will permanently provide companies, business trusts and variable capital companies with the option of conducting fully virtual or hybrid meetings through the use of technology.
